job.style: a description of a classroom activity or experiment and what it shows

response.passage: In our physics lab, we conducted four experiments to understand energy and work. First, Rohan pushed against a heavy concrete pillar for ten minutes until he was sweating and exhausted, yet the pillar did not move an inch. Second, a student carried a heavy bag horizontally across the room at a constant speed. Third, we observed a ball rolling on a rough floor until it gradually slowed down and stopped due to friction, which converted its motion into heat. Finally, we compared two motors lifting the same weight to the same height; the first motor took ten seconds, while the second took twenty seconds. We learned that scientific work requires both force and displacement in the direction of force. Energy is never destroyed; it simply changes form, such as kinetic energy turning into heat. Furthermore, the rate of doing work is defined as power, meaning the faster motor is more powerful, even if the total work done is identical. We also noted that energy is a property of all objects, not just living things, and it is conserved throughout these processes.
response.summary: This experiment demonstrates that scientific work requires displacement and that energy is conserved rather than destroyed. It also clarifies that power measures the rate of work, while energy exists in all objects.
